editorial:
You get pulled into a creepy small-town mystery. When Jamie Ashen's wife is brutally murdered after a strange package arrives at their door, he heads back to his hometown of Raven's Fair to find answers. The package holds a ventriloquist dummy named Billy, and it may connect to the legend of Mary Shaw, a performer killed by angry locals years ago. The movie has a dark, gothic feel, with foggy streets, old theaters, and a sense of being watched. Jamie is a determined but shaken hero, and a suspicious detective keeps the tension high.

The standout is the atmosphere. Director James Wan builds dread through silence, shadows, and unsettling dummy faces. The sound design is clever, using quiet moments to make every creak feel huge. On the downside, some characters make dumb choices, and scares feel predictable. The pacing drags in the middle before the finale kicks in. The twist ending lands hard and makes the story click. This is a great pick for fans of supernatural horror and creepy doll movies. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture and sound.
endingExplained: In the final act, Jamie discovers his father Edward has been turned into a ventriloquist dummy by Mary Shaw. He returns home, where Detective Lipton arrives to arrest him. But Lipton is also one of Shaw's dolls, and Jamie screams in terror. Mary Shaw rips out his tongue, killing him. The last shot reveals Jamie, his wife Lisa, and his father Edward all sitting as dummies in Shaw's collection. The twist is that Mary Shaw won completely, turning everyone Jamie loved into her puppets.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves creepy doll horror and twist endings.
